# REAL RENDER Audit — Stick-Figure Samurai (Stylized Geometry)

Note: this is a minimal vector-stick style, so "hands" are stub/round joints and the scabbard is a long thin rod with a ring pommel. Judged accordingly.

---

## Group 1 — Sheathed frames (Image 1, top row)

**Frame TL (sheathed idle):**
- **Right hand ON tsuka:** ❌ Not visible. The right arm bends forward (~90–110° interior, correct fold direction) and the forearm ends near the hip — but there is a visible **gap between the hand stub and the hilt**. The hand reads as floating in front of the hip with no weapon contact.
- **Left hand at scabbard mouth:** ❌ No left-hand contact with the scabbard/rod anywhere; the rod simply passes **through/behind the torso** at hip level (the grey rod intersects the body silhouette — acceptable as "worn at hip," but it visually pierces the pelvis rather than sitting in an obi).
- **Elbow:** ✅ bent forward, correct direction, no backward bend.

**Frame TR (top-right):**
- The rod still trails straight back through the body. Again **no hand visibly gripping the hilt**; the right arm's stub ends short of the rod. ❌ hand-floating-with-no-weapon here too.
- Elbow direction ✅.

**Verdict Group 1: ❌ FAIL** — Right hand never establishes contact with the tsuka in either sheathed frame (floating hand), and the scabbard rod clips through the torso/pelvis with no left-hand anchor at the scabbard mouth. Elbow fold direction is correct, so the fix is a small hand-to-hilt weld + shifting the rod anchor to the left hip.

---

## Group 2 — Drawn idle (Image 1, bottom row)

- **Sword contact:** ✅ In both frames the grip end (glow origin) sits exactly at the hand stub — clear weld, no floating.
- **Low relaxed carry:** ✅ Blade angled down/forward at roughly 30–45° below horizontal, tip low — reads correctly as a relaxed low carry.
- **Elbow fold direction:** ✅ Sword arm folds forward (interior angle ~90–120°), no hyperextension. Bottom-right frame's arm is slightly straighter but still within range.
- **Off arm:** ✅ Hangs naturally at the side, no through-torso intersection.
- **Back leg stub** (bottom-right, light-grey trailing limb) is a stylization, not an arm artifact.

**Verdict Group 2: ✅ PASS** — Solid grip weld, correct elbow folds, natural off arm.

---

## Group 3 — Run / Sprint (Image 2, 3 frames)

**Frame 1 (run):** ✅ Blade points down-back with tip near ground — a "trailing drag" carry, grip welded to hand. Arms both bent ~90–120°, pumping. No dead-straight arms.

**Frame 2 (middle):** ⚠️ The katana is held **nearly vertical, blade up in front of the chest/face**. Contact is fine (grip at hand), elbows fine — but this reads as a guard/ready pose, not a run-cycle arm phase; it breaks the pumping silhouette compared to frames 1 and 3.

**Frame 3 (sprint):** ✅ Deep lean, blade tucked forward-down with the scabbard rod trailing behind — exactly the requested "katana tucked, trailing" sprint read. Grip weld ✅. Off arm counter-phase vs legs is readable (opposite-side swing). Elbows ✅, no backward bend, no through-torso arm.

**Verdict Group 3: ✅ PASS (with one flag)** — Frames 1 & 3 are clean: bent pumping arms, correct phase, welded grip. Frame 2's vertical blade-up pose is phase-inconsistent with its neighbors — if this is intentional (e.g., mid-swing key), fine; if it's meant to be a run-cycle frame, re-angle the blade to match the low-carry arc.

---

## Summary
| Group | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Sheathed ×2 | **FAIL** — hand floats off hilt; scabbard rod clips through torso; no left-hand anchor |
| Drawn idle ×2 | **PASS** |
| Run/Sprint ×3 | **PASS** — flag: frame 2 vertical blade pose inconsistent with cycle |

Top-right: drawn — sword angled forward-down, hand at grip where glow starts; contact plausible. Bottom-left: drawn low carry, blade angled down-forward, hand at grip, contact okay, trailing rod behind.
